As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Garbali, Cengiz Gazi, Jan de Gier, William Mead, Michael Wheeler

item.title: Tilted Solid-On-Solid is liquid: scaling limit of SOS with a potential on a slope
item.description:
arXiv:2409.08745v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $(2+1)$D Solid-On-Solid (SOS) model famously exhibits a roughening transition: on an $N	imes N$ torus with the height at the origin rooted at $0$, the variance of $h(x)$, the height at $x$, is $O(1)$ at large inverse-temperature $ eta$, vs $\asymp \log |x|$ at small $ eta$ (as in the Gaussian free field (GFF)). The former--rigidity at large $ eta$--is known for a wide class of $|
abla\phi|^p$ models ($p=1$ being SOS) yet is believed to fail once the surface is on a slope (tilted boundary conditions). It is conjectured that the slope would destabilize the rigidity and induce the GFF-type behavior of the surface at small $ eta$. The only rigorous result on this is by Sheffield '05: for these models of integer height functions, if the slope $	heta$ is irrational, then Var$(h(x))	o\infty$ with $|x|$ (with no known quantitative bound). We study a family of SOS surfaces at a large enough fixed $ eta$, on an $N	imes N$ torus with a nonzero boundary condition slope $	heta$, perturbed by a potential $V$ on an $\epsilon_ eta$-fraction of sites (arbitrarily small). Our main result is (a) the measure on the height gradients $
abla h$ has a limit $\mu_\infty$ as $N	o\infty$; and (b) the scaling limit of a sample from $\mu_\infty$ converges to a full plane GFF. In particular, we recover the asymptotics Var$(h(x))\sim c\log|x|$. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a tilted $|
abla\phi|^p$ model, or a perturbation thereof, where the limit is recovered at large $ eta$. The proof looks at random monotone surfaces that approximate the SOS surface, and shows that (i) these form a weakly interacting dimer model, and (ii) the renormalization framework of Giuliani, Mastropietro and Toninelli '17 leads to the GFF limit. New ingredients are needed in both parts, including a nontrivial extension of [GMT17] from finite interactions to ones with exponential decay in the radius.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Laslier, Eyal Lubetzky

item.title: Sturm-Liouville problems on graphs with Robin boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2510.23392v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study characteristic functions and describe asymptotics of the eigenvalues for the spectral Sturm-Liouville problem on graphs equipped with Robin-Kirhhoff boundary conditions. Also, we show how to recover the coefficients in the Robin conditions for the quantum graphs provided the shape of the graphs and some Robin eigenvalues are known.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Latushkin, Vyacheslav Pivovarchik, Alesia Supranovych

item.title: Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations: exact exponents and scaling limits
item.description: arXiv:2510.26123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study longest and shortest directed paths in the following natural model of directed random planar maps: the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation (UIBOT), which is the local limit of uniform bipolar-oriented triangulations around a typical edge. We construct the Busemann function which measures directed distance to $\infty$ along a natural interface in the UIBOT. We show that in the case of longest (resp.\ shortest) directed paths, this Busemann function converges in the scaling limit to a $2/3$-stable L\'evy process (resp.\ a $4/3$-stable L\'evy process). We also prove up-to-constants bounds for directed distances in finite bipolar-oriented triangulations sampled from a Boltzmann distribution, and for size-$n$ cells in the UIBOT. These bounds imply that in a typical subset of the UIBOT with $n$ edges, longest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/4}$ and shortest directed path lengths are of order $n^{3/8}$. These results give the scaling dimensions for discretizations of the (hypothetical) $\sqrt{4/3}$-directed Liouville quantum gravity metrics. The main external input in our proof is the bijection of Kenyon-Miller-Sheffield-Wilson (2015). We do not use any continuum theory. We expect that our techniques can also be applied to prove similar results for directed distances in other random planar map models and for longest increasing subsequences in pattern-avoiding permutations.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Ewain Gwynne

item.title: A fast and rigorous numerical tool to measure length-scale artifacts in molecular simulations
item.description: arXiv:2511.01442v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality for classical and quantum many-body systems is a theorem that provides rigorous bounds on the free-energy cost of partitioning a given system into two or more independent subsystems. This theorem motivates the definition of a quality factor which directly quantifies the degree of statistical-mechanical consistency achieved by a given simulation box size. A major technical merit of the theorem is that, for systems with two-body interactions and a known radial distribution function, the quality factor can be computed by evaluating just three six-dimensional integrals. We present a numerical algorithm for computing the quality factor and demonstrate its consistency with respect to results in the literature obtained from simulations performed at different box sizes.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt M. Reible, Nils Liebreich, Carsten Hartmann, Luigi Delle Site

item.title: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
item.description: arXiv:2511.15876v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators. Furthermore, using the universal TT-relations we derive exchange relations between spin-j Hamiltonians and the two non-local operators showing non-trivial symmetries for special boundary conditions, that they commute with all Hamiltonian densities. As another application of our universal TT-relations we propose universal T-system, Y-system and universal TQ-relations for $A_q$, and as a result, universal TQ for the q-Onsager algebra. For diagonal boundary conditions, we also obtain universal TT- and TQ-relations for a degenerate version of $A_q$ known as centrally extended augmented q-Onsager algebra. We finally discuss implications of our results for generalized Gibbs ensemble construction.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Baseilhac, Azat M. Gainutdinov, Guillaume Lemarthe

item.title: Quantum optimal control of steady orbits
item.description: arXiv:2606.15383v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Periodically driven dissipative systems can settle into steady orbits - fixed infinite loops on their dynamical manifolds. In quantum mechanics, steady orbits occur in cooling engines, lasers and masers, precision metrology devices, and magnetic resonance. Steady orbits and stroboscopic steady states are a promising target for quantum optimal control, but the numerical complexity is prohibitive: infinite loops defeat state-of-the-art algorithms that use explicit numerical propagation in the time domain. We report a solution to this problem and introduce a numerically efficient quantum optimal control algorithm for steady orbits. We use this algorithm to design microwave pulse sequences that dynamically polarise nuclear spins and enhance their magnetic resonance signals, while taking into account instrumental distortions. Improved performance relative to leading current methods is demonstrated experimentally.
item.dc:creator: Shebha Anandhi Jegadeesan, Yujie Zhao, Robert Hunter, Hassane El Mkami, Maximilian Keitel, Callum Musselwhite, Graham Smith, Guinevere Mathies, Ilya Kuprov

item.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
item.description: arXiv:2608.13644v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we introduce a method for searching for entanglement distillation protocols and, using this technique, distil qubit Werner states at a higher rate than could be achieved using previously discovered protocols. In particular, we demonstrate the advantage of our new distillation strategy by improving the best known lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarising channel across a wide range of channel parameters, making progress in one of the long-standing problems of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Novel lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.16296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We apply the generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations to construct second-order two- and three-lump solutions and third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation. We determine the long-time positions and amplitudes of these degenerate lumps and show that their anomalous scattering produces asymptotic amplitude corrections that differ from those in the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Multiparameter Quantum Affine Spaces and the Scalene Yang--Baxter Equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.20714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct representation-independent families of solutions of the non-braided scalene Yang--Baxter equation from quadratic noncommutative algebras. Beginning with two anticommuting generators, we obtain a continuous deformation in terms of quantum-plane algebras and extend the construction to an arbitrary number of generators. In the latter case the scalene Yang--Baxter relation fixes the multiparameter exchange matrix to an exact multiplicative form, thereby selecting a distinguished subclass of multiparameter quantum affine spaces. We construct finite-dimensional realizations using singular matrices and finite Heisenberg--Weyl operators, as well as infinite-dimensional realizations in terms of bilateral weighted shifts and multiplicative-shift operators. The explicit realizations are generically weakly purely scalene: their individual constituent operators do not satisfy the ordinary constant non-braided Yang--Baxter equation. For selected finite-dimensional realizations, we additionally establish strong purity by obstructing a generic common meromorphic Yang--Baxter parametrization, even up to consistent invertible local similarities and nonzero scalar rescalings. These results provide a representation-independent algebraic framework for constructing scalene triples and a starting point for investigating their possible applications to quantum integrability.
item.dc:creator: Pramod Padmanabhan, Somnath Maity, Vladimir Korepin

item.title: Open Inextensible Filaments in Planar Stokes Flow: Well-Posedness, Endpoint Asymptotics, and Straightening
item.description: arXiv:2609.10480v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study an inextensible open filament with free ends in a planar Stokes fluid. The system reduces to a third-order nonlocal curvature equation coupled to an elliptic equation for the tension. We prove local well-posedness for nearly critical initial data in supported Sobolev spaces $\widetilde H^s$, $-1/2<s\le0$, satisfying the arc-chord condition. For positive times, we prove improved Sobolev regularity and derive a $d^{3/2}$-type expansion at each free end using Wiener--Hopf factorization, where $d$ denotes the distance to that endpoint. We further prove global existence and exponential convergence to a straight filament for sufficiently small initial data and for finite-energy initial data satisfying $E(0)<\pi^2/4$. The finite-energy result follows from an energy identity and a geometric estimate relating the bending energy to the arc-chord constant. More generally, any finite-time breakdown must be accompanied by loss of the arc-chord condition, while every global solution either converges exponentially to a straight filament or has arc-chord constants tending to zero along a sequence of times tending to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Han Zhou

item.title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
item.description: arXiv:2609.27792v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibres, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel's two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Exact anomalous current fluctuations in the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain
item.description: arXiv:2609.37512v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study spin-current fluctuations of the folded XXZ chain, which describes the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain. We obtain an exact expression for the moment-generating function of the time-integrated spin current at infinite temperature. A long-time asymptotic analysis establishes that the rescaled time-integrated current converges to a non-Gaussian distribution described by the M-Wright function. The derivation relies on a nonlocal map to the one-dimensional t-0 model and its exact spin-charge separation. By extending this approach, we also show that the dynamical correlation function of the spins summed over two adjacent sites exhibits a diffusive Gaussian profile at long times.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Ishiyama, Taiga Kurose, Kazuya Fujimoto, Tomohiro Sasamoto

item.title: Fer expansion of driven spins: closed-form recursion and no-go theorems for termination
item.description: arXiv:2610.27979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fer expansion factorizes the propagator of a driven quantum system into exponentials of time-integrated effective Hamiltonians, which govern the evolution left over by the previous factors. Every truncation is unitary, and adding a factor squares the size of the remainder, but each effective Hamiltonian is an infinite series of nested commutators of the previous one. For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, in every representation, from qubits to spins of any dimension, we represent the effective Hamiltonians by time-dependent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and resum this series exactly. The result is a closed map from one vector to the next, in which the infinite series reduces to the previous vector crossed once and twice with its time integral, weighted by elementary functions. Using this map, we address the question of when the expansion can be stopped after finitely many factors. This is possible whenever the leftover evolution is known in closed form, for instance when the effective Hamiltonian commutes with itself at all times or precesses about a fixed axis with constant angular velocity. We prove that, for real-analytic drives, neither happens beyond the first factor unless the first exponential is already exact. Stopping the expansion therefore yields no new exactly solvable drives.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Daniel Burgarth, Vittorio Giovannetti, Kazuya Yuasa

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38584v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin
